blocks.en: The Lamb Opens the Seals
blocks.es_reference: El Cordero Abre los Sellos

blocks.en: Chapter five ended with the Lamb taking the sealed scroll from the hand of God; now He begins to open it. This is the first thing to notice, and it governs the whole chapter: it is the Lamb who breaks the seals. The judgments that follow are not the work of blind fate or of an enemy out of control, but unfold only as the slain and risen Lamb opens them, one by one, under His sovereign hand. Christians have read the seals in different ways — some seeing them fulfilled in the first centuries, some across the long span of history, some as describing a final period still to come, and some as a picture of the recurring troubles of every age. The course has set those approaches side by side already and will not press one here. What every faithful reading shares is the comfort that nothing breaks loose upon the world except by the hand of the Lamb who loves His people and was found worthy to open the scroll of history.
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo cinco terminó con el Cordero tomando el libro sellado de la mano de Dios; ahora comienza a abrirlo. Esto es lo primero que hay que notar, y gobierna todo el capítulo: es el Cordero quien rompe los sellos. Los juicios que siguen no son obra de un destino ciego ni de un enemigo fuera de control, sino que se despliegan solo a medida que el Cordero inmolado y resucitado los abre, uno por uno, bajo su mano soberana. Los cristianos han leído los sellos de diferentes maneras — viendo algunos su cumplimiento en los primeros siglos, algunos a lo largo de la historia, algunos como descripción de un período final aún por venir, y algunos como una imagen de los problemas recurrentes de cada época. El curso ya ha puesto esos enfoques lado a lado y no insistirá en uno aquí. Lo que toda lectura fiel comparte es el consuelo de que nada se desata sobre el mundo sino por la mano del Cordero que ama a su pueblo y fue hallado digno de abrir el libro de la historia.

blocks.en: The Four Horsemen: Conquest, War, Famine, Death
blocks.es_reference: Los Cuatro Jinetes: Conquista, Guerra, Hambre, Muerte

blocks.en: As the first four seals are opened, four horses and their riders ride out. The first is a white horse whose rider holds a bow, is given a crown, and goes out "conquering and to conquer" (Revelation 6:2). This rider has been understood in two main ways: some take him as Christ or the advance of the gospel going out in triumph, while others take him as a spirit of conquest or a false christ, and the course leaves the matter open. The second is a red horse, whose rider is granted power to "take peace from the earth, and that people should kill one another," and is given a great sword (Revelation 6:4) — this is war and slaughter. The third is a black horse, whose rider holds a pair of scales, and a voice prices a day's wheat at a day's wage — this is famine and crushing scarcity, while the oil and the wine are spared. The fourth is a pale, ashen horse, "and the name of him who sat on it was Death, and Hades followed with him" (Revelation 6:8). It is a haunting picture: Death rides the pale horse, and the grave comes close behind like a hearse, given power over a fourth of the earth to kill with sword, with hunger, with plague, and by the beasts of the earth. The four horsemen gather up the great recurring woes of a fallen world under the judgment of God.
blocks.es_reference: Al abrirse los primeros cuatro sellos, salen cuatro caballos y sus jinetes. El primero es un caballo blanco cuyo jinete tiene un arco, recibe una corona, y sale "venciendo, y para vencer" (Apocalipsis 6:2). Este jinete se ha entendido de dos maneras principales: algunos lo toman como Cristo o el avance del evangelio que sale en triunfo, mientras que otros lo toman como un espíritu de conquista o un falso cristo, y el curso deja el asunto abierto. El segundo es un caballo bermejo, cuyo jinete recibe poder para "quitar la paz de la tierra, y que se maten unos a otros," y se le da una gran espada (Apocalipsis 6:4) — esto es guerra y matanza. El tercero es un caballo negro, cuyo jinete tiene una balanza en su mano, y una voz pone el precio de un día de trigo en un día de salario — esto es hambre y escasez aplastante, mientras que el aceite y el vino se libran. El cuarto es un caballo amarillo y pálido, "y el que estaba sentado sobre él tenía por nombre Muerte; y el infierno le seguía" (Apocalipsis 6:8). Es una imagen estremecedora: la Muerte cabalga el caballo pálido, y la tumba viene cerca detrás como un coche fúnebre, con poder sobre la cuarta parte de la tierra para matar con espada, con hambre, con mortandad, y por las fieras de la tierra. Los cuatro jinetes reúnen las grandes calamidades recurrentes de un mundo caído bajo el juicio de Dios.

blocks.en: The Fifth Seal: The Cry of the Martyrs
blocks.es_reference: El Quinto Sello: El Clamor de los Mártires

blocks.en: When the Lamb opens the fifth seal, the scene shifts from earth to the altar in heaven. "I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony which they held" (Revelation 6:9). These are the martyrs, those put to death for their faithfulness to Christ, and they cry out with a loud voice, "How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?" (Revelation 6:10). It is not a cry of personal revenge but a longing that God would set the world right and vindicate His own. They are given white robes, the dress of purity and acceptance, and they are told to "rest a little longer, until both the number of their fellow servants and their brethren, who would be killed as they were, was completed" (Revelation 6:11). The answer is tender but sobering: justice is certain, but not yet; more of God's servants will yet suffer, and the martyrs are to rest in God's timing until the full number is gathered.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando el Cordero abre el quinto sello, la escena cambia de la tierra al altar en el cielo. "Vi debajo del altar las almas de los que habían sido muertos por causa de la palabra de Dios, y por el testimonio que ellos tenían" (Apocalipsis 6:9). Estos son los mártires, los que fueron muertos por su fidelidad a Cristo, y claman a gran voz: "¿Hasta cuándo, Señor, santo y verdadero, no juzgas y vengas nuestra sangre de los que moran en la tierra?" (Apocalipsis 6:10). No es un clamor de venganza personal sino un anhelo de que Dios enderece el mundo y vindique a los suyos. Se les dan ropas blancas, el vestido de la pureza y la aceptación, y se les dice que "reposasen todavía un poco de tiempo, hasta que se completara el número de sus consiervos y de sus hermanos, que también habían de ser muertos como ellos" (Apocalipsis 6:11). La respuesta es tierna pero seria: la justicia es cierta, pero no todavía; más de los siervos de Dios aún sufrirán, y los mártires han de reposar en el tiempo de Dios hasta que se reúna el número completo.

blocks.en: The Sixth Seal: The Great Day of Wrath
blocks.es_reference: El Sexto Sello: El Gran Día de la Ira

blocks.en: The sixth seal brings a violent shaking of the whole created order. There is a great earthquake; "the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became like blood"; the stars of heaven fall like late figs shaken from a tree; the sky recedes "as a scroll when it is rolled up"; and every mountain and island is moved out of its place (Revelation 6:12-14). The reaction on earth is universal terror. Kings, great men, commanders, the rich and the mighty, and every slave and free man hide themselves in caves and among the rocks, and they cry to the mountains and rocks, "Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb! For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?" (Revelation 6:16-17). Notice that even the wrath is the wrath of the Lamb; the same gentle Lamb who was slain is also the holy Judge whose day no sinner can face. The chapter ends on that desperate question, "Who is able to stand?" — and it is exactly that question that chapter seven steps in to answer.
blocks.es_reference: El sexto sello trae una violenta sacudida de todo el orden creado. Hay un gran terremoto; "el sol se puso negro como un saco de cilicio, y la luna se volvió toda como sangre"; las estrellas del cielo caen como higos tardíos sacudidos de un árbol; el cielo se retira "como un pergamino que se enrolla"; y todo monte e isla es removido de su lugar (Apocalipsis 6:12-14). La reacción en la tierra es de terror universal. Los reyes, los grandes, los capitanes, los ricos y los poderosos, y todo siervo y libre se esconden en cuevas y entre las rocas, y claman a los montes y a las rocas: "Caed sobre nosotros, y escondednos del rostro de aquel que está sentado sobre el trono, y de la ira del Cordero; porque el gran día de su ira ha venido; ¿y quién podrá estar en pie?" (Apocalipsis 6:16-17). Nótese que aun la ira es la ira del Cordero; el mismo Cordero manso que fue inmolado es también el Juez santo cuyo día ningún pecador puede enfrentar. El capítulo termina con esa pregunta desesperada, "¿quién podrá estar en pie?" — y es exactamente esa pregunta la que el capítulo siete entra a responder.

blocks.en: The Interlude: The 144,000 Sealed
blocks.es_reference: El Interludio: Los Ciento Cuarenta y Cuatro Mil Sellados

blocks.en: Between the sixth seal and the seventh comes a pause, and in it John sees two scenes of God's protected people. In the first, four angels hold back the four winds of judgment until the servants of God are sealed. "And I heard the number of those who were sealed. One hundred and forty-four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel were sealed" (Revelation 7:4), twelve thousand from each of twelve tribes. To be sealed on the forehead is to be marked as God's own and kept safe through what is coming, just as Israel was marked before the plagues fell on Egypt. Who exactly the 144,000 are has been understood in several ways — some take them as literal Israel, some as the church as the true Israel of God, and some as a faithful remnant — and the number itself is read by some as exact and by others as a symbol of completeness, twelve times twelve times a thousand. The course presents these views fairly. The point all share is clear and comforting: before the storm of judgment fully breaks, God sets His seal upon His servants, and not one of them is overlooked.
blocks.es_reference: Entre el sexto sello y el séptimo viene una pausa, y en ella Juan ve dos escenas del pueblo protegido de Dios. En la primera, cuatro ángeles detienen los cuatro vientos del juicio hasta que los siervos de Dios sean sellados. "Y oí el número de los que fueron sellados: ciento cuarenta y cuatro mil sellados de todas las tribus de los hijos de Israel" (Apocalipsis 7:4), doce mil de cada una de las doce tribus. Ser sellado en la frente es ser marcado como propiedad de Dios y guardado a salvo a través de lo que viene, así como Israel fue marcado antes de que las plagas cayeran sobre Egipto. Quiénes son exactamente los ciento cuarenta y cuatro mil se ha entendido de varias maneras — algunos los toman como el Israel literal, algunos como la iglesia como el verdadero Israel de Dios, y algunos como un remanente fiel — y el número mismo lo leen unos como exacto y otros como un símbolo de plenitud, doce por doce por mil. El curso presenta estas visiones con justicia. El punto que todas comparten es claro y consolador: antes de que la tormenta del juicio estalle del todo, Dios pone su sello sobre sus siervos, y ninguno de ellos es pasado por alto.

blocks.en: The Interlude: The Great Multitude
blocks.es_reference: El Interludio: La Gran Multitud

blocks.en: The second scene lifts John's eyes from the sealed servants on earth to a vast throng in heaven. "After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands" (Revelation 7:9). They cry out, "Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!" (Revelation 7:10). When John asks who they are, an elder tells him, "These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation, and washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb" (Revelation 7:14). Their robes are white not by their own effort but by the blood of the Lamb that cleanses from sin. And their future is glorious: they serve God day and night in His temple; they hunger and thirst no more; the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and lead them to living fountains of waters; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes (Revelation 7:15-17). This is the answer to the sixth seal's question. Who is able to stand? These are: the countless redeemed of every nation, washed in the blood of the Lamb, standing before the throne.
blocks.es_reference: La segunda escena levanta los ojos de Juan de los siervos sellados en la tierra a una vasta muchedumbre en el cielo. "Después de estas cosas miré, y he aquí una gran multitud, la cual ninguno podía contar, de todas naciones y tribus y pueblos y lenguas, que estaban delante del trono y en la presencia del Cordero, vestidos de ropas blancas, y con palmas en sus manos" (Apocalipsis 7:9). Claman: "Salvación a nuestro Dios que está sentado sobre el trono, y al Cordero" (Apocalipsis 7:10). Cuando Juan pregunta quiénes son, un anciano le dice: "Estos son los que han salido de la gran tribulación, y han lavado sus ropas, y las han blanqueado en la sangre del Cordero" (Apocalipsis 7:14). Sus ropas son blancas no por su propio esfuerzo sino por la sangre del Cordero que limpia del pecado. Y su futuro es glorioso: sirven a Dios día y noche en su templo; no tienen más hambre ni sed; el Cordero que está en medio del trono los pastoreará y los guiará a fuentes vivas de aguas; y Dios enjugará toda lágrima de los ojos de ellos (Apocalipsis 7:15-17). Esta es la respuesta a la pregunta del sexto sello. ¿Quién podrá estar en pie? Estos pueden: los incontables redimidos de toda nación, lavados en la sangre del Cordero, en pie delante del trono.

blocks.en: The Seventh Seal: Silence in Heaven
blocks.es_reference: El Séptimo Sello: Silencio en el Cielo

blocks.en: After the long interlude, the Lamb opens the last seal. "When He opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour" (Revelation 8:1). After the thunder of the horsemen, the cry of the martyrs, the shaking of the sixth seal, and the great shouts of the multitude, heaven falls utterly still. The silence is full of awe and expectation, the hush before God's purposes move forward into the next great cycle of visions, for in that silence seven angels are given seven trumpets, which the next unit will take up. Read together, the seven seals teach a steadying truth. The judgments of history fall only as the Lamb opens them; the martyrs are heard and will be vindicated in God's time; God seals and secures His own before the storm; and the redeemed of every nation, washed in the Lamb's blood, stand at last before the throne. The world may be shaken to its foundations, but the Lamb holds the scroll, and His people are safe in His hand.
blocks.es_reference: Después del largo interludio, el Cordero abre el último sello. "Cuando él abrió el séptimo sello, fue hecho silencio en el cielo como por media hora" (Apocalipsis 8:1). Después del trueno de los jinetes, el clamor de los mártires, la sacudida del sexto sello, y las grandes voces de la multitud, el cielo queda completamente quieto. El silencio está lleno de asombro y expectación, la pausa antes de que los propósitos de Dios avancen al siguiente gran ciclo de visiones, pues en ese silencio se dan a siete ángeles siete trompetas, que la siguiente unidad tomará. Leídos juntos, los siete sellos enseñan una verdad que afirma. Los juicios de la historia caen solo a medida que el Cordero los abre; los mártires son oídos y serán vindicados en el tiempo de Dios; Dios sella y asegura a los suyos antes de la tormenta; y los redimidos de toda nación, lavados en la sangre del Cordero, están al fin delante del trono. El mundo puede ser sacudido hasta sus cimientos, pero el Cordero tiene el libro, y su pueblo está seguro en su mano.

mc.stem: The seven seals on the scroll are opened by:
mc.why: The Lamb, found worthy in chapter 5, opens the seals (6:1).

mc.stem: The fact that the Lamb opens the seals teaches that the judgments:
options: Are the work of blind fate
Unfold only as the Lamb opens them, under His control
Cannot be stopped by anyone, including God
mc.why: Nothing breaks loose except by the hand of the Lamb (6:1).

mc.stem: The rider on the white horse (first seal) carried a bow and was given:
mc.why: He was given a crown and went out conquering and to conquer (6:2).

mc.stem: The rider on the red horse (second seal) was given power to:
options: Take peace from the earth, with a great sword
mc.why: He takes peace from the earth so people kill one another — war (6:4).

mc.stem: The black horse and its rider's pair of scales picture:
mc.why: The scales and the priced grain picture famine and scarcity (6:5-6).

mc.stem: The rider on the pale horse is named ___, and ___ followed close behind:
mc.why: "His name was Death, and Hades followed with him" (6:8).

mc.stem: The four horsemen were given power over what portion of the earth?
mc.why: Power was given over a fourth of the earth to kill (6:8).

mc.stem: When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, under the altar John saw:
options: The souls of those slain for the word of God
mc.why: The souls of the martyrs, slain for the word of God (6:9).

mc.stem: The martyrs under the altar cried out, asking God:
options: To send them back to earth
How long until You judge and avenge our blood
To end the world at once
mc.why: "How long... until You judge and avenge our blood?" (6:10).

mc.stem: The martyrs were given white robes and told to:
options: Rest a little longer, until the full number was complete
mc.why: Rest a little longer until the number of fellow servants is complete (6:11).

mc.stem: The sixth seal brought:
options: A great earthquake, a blackened sun, a blood-red moon, falling stars
mc.why: A violent cosmic upheaval shakes the whole created order (6:12-14).

mc.stem: At the sixth seal, kings and all people hid and begged the mountains to hide them from:
options: The face of Him on the throne and the wrath of the Lamb
mc.why: They hid from Him on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb (6:16).

mc.stem: The desperate question that ends the sixth seal is:
mc.why: "The great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?" (6:17).

mc.stem: Between the sixth and seventh seals, the interlude of chapter 7 shows God:
options: Sealing and securing His servants before judgment
mc.why: The winds are held back while God's servants are sealed (7:1-3).

mc.stem: The 144,000 were sealed from:
options: The twelve tribes of the children of Israel
mc.why: 144,000, twelve thousand from each of the twelve tribes of Israel (7:4).

mc.stem: The lesson presents the identity of the 144,000 as understood in several ways. Which is NOT one of them?
options: A meaningless number invented at random
The church as the true Israel of God
mc.why: The three readings are real; the random/meaningless option is not (7:4).

mc.stem: The great multitude that no one could number came from:
options: All nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues
mc.why: A multitude from every nation, tribe, people, and tongue (7:9).

mc.stem: The great multitude had come out of the great tribulation and had washed their robes white in:
mc.why: They washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb (7:14).

mc.stem: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was:
options: Silence in heaven for about half an hour
mc.why: Silence in heaven for about half an hour (8:1).

mc.stem: The central comfort of the interlude, answering "who is able to stand?", is that:
options: God's redeemed, sealed and washed in the Lamb's blood, stand before the throne
mc.why: The sealed, blood-washed redeemed are the ones who can stand (7:9-17).

sa.prompt: Why is it significant that the Lamb is the One who opens the seals?
sa.model: It is the Lamb, found worthy in chapter five, who opens the seven seals, and this governs how the whole chapter is read. The judgments that follow are not the work of blind fate, nor of an enemy out of control, nor a sign that history has slipped from God's hand. They unfold only as the slain and risen Lamb opens them, one by one, under His sovereign control. This is a deep comfort to a suffering church, for it means that nothing breaks loose upon the world except by the hand of the Lamb who loves His people and was found worthy to open the scroll of history. Christians have read the seals in different ways, some seeing them in the first centuries, some across all history, some as a final period, and some as the recurring troubles of every age, and the course does not press one. What every faithful reading shares is the assurance that the Lamb, not chaos, holds the scroll and directs the judgments of God.

sa.prompt: Describe the four horsemen of the first four seals and what each represents.
sa.model: As the first four seals are opened, four horses ride out. The first is a white horse whose rider holds a bow and is given a crown and goes out conquering; some take this rider as Christ or the advancing gospel and others as a spirit of conquest or a false christ, and the course leaves it open. The second is a red horse whose rider takes peace from the earth so that people kill one another and is given a great sword, which is war and slaughter. The third is a black horse whose rider holds a pair of scales while a voice prices grain at a day's wage, which is famine and crushing scarcity. The fourth is a pale, ashen horse whose rider is named Death, with Hades following close behind like a hearse, given power over a fourth of the earth to kill by sword, famine, plague, and wild beasts. Together the four horsemen gather up the great recurring woes of a fallen world under the judgment of God.

sa.prompt: Describe the fifth seal: the martyrs under the altar, their cry, and the answer they were given.
sa.model: At the fifth seal the scene shifts to the altar in heaven, where John sees under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for their testimony. These are the martyrs, put to death for their faithfulness to Christ. They cry with a loud voice, How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth. It is not a cry of personal revenge but a longing that God would set the world right and vindicate His own. Each of them is given a white robe, the dress of purity and acceptance, and they are told to rest a little longer, until the number of their fellow servants and brethren who would also be killed was complete. The answer is tender but sobering: their vindication is certain, but not yet, for more of God's servants will still suffer, and the martyrs are to rest in God's perfect timing until the full number of the redeemed is gathered.

sa.prompt: Describe the sixth seal and explain the question "who is able to stand?"
sa.model: The sixth seal brings a violent shaking of the whole created order. There is a great earthquake, the sun turns black as sackcloth, the moon becomes like blood, the stars fall like figs shaken from a tree, the sky recedes like a rolled-up scroll, and every mountain and island is moved from its place. The reaction on earth is universal terror. Kings, great men, commanders, the rich, the mighty, and every slave and free man hide in caves and among the rocks and beg the mountains to fall on them and hide them from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb. It is striking that even the wrath is called the wrath of the Lamb, for the same gentle Lamb who was slain is also the holy Judge whose day no sinner can face. The seal ends with the desperate question, the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand. The question hangs unanswered until chapter seven steps in to answer it with the picture of God's sealed and redeemed people.

sa.prompt: Explain the sealing of the 144,000 in the interlude, including the ways their identity has been understood.
sa.model: In the first scene of the interlude, four angels hold back the four winds of judgment until the servants of God are sealed. John hears the number of those sealed: one hundred forty-four thousand from all the tribes of the children of Israel, twelve thousand from each of twelve tribes. To be sealed on the forehead is to be marked as God's own and kept safe through what is coming, much as Israel was marked before the plagues fell on Egypt. Who exactly the 144,000 are has been understood in several ways: some take them as literal Israel, some as the church as the true Israel of God, and some as a faithful remnant, while the number itself is read by some as exact and by others as a symbol of completeness, twelve times twelve times a thousand. The course presents these views fairly without insisting on one. The point they all share is clear and comforting: before the storm of judgment fully breaks, God sets His seal upon His servants to protect them, and not one of them is overlooked or lost.

sa.prompt: Describe the great multitude of Revelation 7: where they came from and what had been done for them.
sa.model: The second scene of the interlude lifts John's eyes to a great multitude which no one could number, drawn from all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes and holding palm branches. They cry out, Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb. When John asks who they are, an elder tells him these are the ones who came out of the great tribulation and washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Their robes are white not by their own effort or merit but by the cleansing blood of the Lamb, which alone takes away sin. They are a worldwide family, gathered from every people on earth, the fruit of the Lamb's redemption. This great multitude is the answer to the sixth seal's question, who is able to stand: these can, the countless redeemed of every nation, washed in the Lamb's blood and standing secure before the throne of God.

sa.prompt: What is promised to the great multitude before the throne (Revelation 7:15-17)?
sa.model: The future promised to the great multitude is glorious. They stand before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple, and the One on the throne will dwell among them. They will hunger no more and thirst no more, and the sun will not strike them nor any scorching heat. The reason is tender and surprising: the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will be their shepherd. The slain Lamb who redeemed them now leads them like a flock, guiding them to living fountains of waters that never run dry. And God Himself will wipe away every tear from their eyes, a promise of comfort so complete that all the sorrow of their tribulation is gone forever. This same promise of no more tears reappears at the very end of the book, in the new heaven and new earth. So the redeemed who came through great tribulation are not merely spared; they are brought into endless joy, fed and led and comforted by the Lamb in the presence of God.

sa.prompt: What happens when the Lamb opens the seventh seal, and what does the silence suggest?
sa.model: After the long interlude, the Lamb opens the last seal, and the result is unexpected: there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. After the thunder of the four horsemen, the cry of the martyrs, the shaking of the sixth seal, and the great shouts of the multitude, heaven falls utterly still. The silence is full of awe and expectation. It is the hush before God's purposes move forward into the next great cycle of visions, for in that silence seven angels are given seven trumpets, which the following unit will take up. The half hour of silence marks a solemn pause, as if all heaven holds its breath before the next stage of judgment. So the seventh seal does not so much end the sequence as open onto the trumpets, joining the seals to what comes next. The silence reminds the reader that these visions move forward only at God's measured pace, under the hand of the Lamb who opened the scroll.

sa.prompt: How does the interlude of chapter 7 answer the terror of the sixth seal?
sa.model: The sixth seal ends with a terrified world hiding from the wrath of the Lamb and crying, who is able to stand. Chapter seven answers that very question. First it shows God sealing the 144,000 of His servants on their foreheads, marking them as His own and securing them before the winds of judgment are loosed, so that His people are protected and not one is overlooked. Then it shows the great multitude that no one could number, drawn from every nation, standing before the throne in white robes, having come out of great tribulation with their robes washed white in the blood of the Lamb. Together the two scenes give the answer: those who can stand are the redeemed people of God, sealed and kept by Him and cleansed by the blood of the Lamb. The unsaved cannot face the day of wrath, but God's own are secure. So the interlude turns the terror of the sixth seal into comfort, assuring the church that judgment falling on the world will not sweep away those who belong to the Lamb.

sa.prompt: Summarize the central truth of Unit 6: what do the seven seals teach the church?
sa.model: The central truth of Unit 6 is a steadying one for a church that suffers. The seven seals teach, first, that the judgments of history fall only as the Lamb opens them, so that conquest, war, famine, and death, terrible as they are, remain under the sovereign hand of the One who was slain. Second, the martyrs under the altar are heard and will be vindicated in God's perfect time, even though more of His servants will yet suffer. Third, when the sixth seal shows the great day of wrath and asks who is able to stand, the interlude answers that God seals and secures His own before the storm, marking His servants and gathering a countless multitude from every nation. Those who stand are the redeemed, washed white in the blood of the Lamb. And the seventh seal opens in silence onto the trumpets to come. The world may be shaken to its foundations, but the Lamb holds the scroll of history, His people are sealed and safe in His hand, and the redeemed of every nation will stand before the throne.
